senses.definition: A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering.
examples: Wipe your feet on the mat before coming in.

senses.definition: A small flat piece of material used to protect a surface from anything hot or rough; a coaster.
examples: They put mats on the table during mealtimes.

senses.definition: (athletics) A floor pad to protect athletes.
examples: The high jumper cleared the bar and landed safely on the mat.

quotes.text: But to return to where we left her, I see her still, propped up in a kind of stupor against one of the walls in which this wretched edifice abounds, her long grey greasy hair framing in its cowl of scrofulous mats a face where pallor, languor, hunger, acne, recent dirt, immemorial chagrin and surplus hair seemed to dispute the mastery.

senses.definition: A thin layer of woven, non-woven, or knitted fiber that serves as reinforcement to a material.
A thin surface layer; superficial cover.
examples: Iceland moss growing in a mat

quotes.text: The fad for blaming all mass extinctions (such as happened at the end of the Cretaceous when the dinosaurs vanished) on impacts of objects from space was extended to the Pleistocene in 2007. That year a group of scientists proposed that the North American extinctions were due to a comet or meteorite impact over the Carolinas, near the beginning of the Younger Dryas event, about 12,900 years ago. The original evidence for this supposed impact was a "black mat" of organic material in many Clovis sites, plus microscopic nano-diamonds in deep-sea cores, and rare Platinum group metals in Greenland ice cores from around 12,900 years ago.
quotes.reference: 2016 November 15, Donald R. Prothero, The Princeton Field Guide to Prehistoric Mammals, page 222:
